title: New Challenges in the High Stakes World of Oil Trading - Oil & Money 2014

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/New Challenges in the High Stakes World of Oil Trading - Oil & Money 2014.docx

speakers: Pierre/Peter (hedge fund oil trader, caption spelling varies)
Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
summary: Oil and Money 2014 panel (Oct-Nov 2014): after the Brent fall, speakers explain a ~2 mb/d supply-demand swing from shale, Libya and weak demand, argue prices fall further before supply and demand cure it, and discuss curve contango and storage, refining and LNG. Conclusion: no stable oil price, product and regional gas dislocations ahead.

coverage.note: Panel intro; Brent/WTI relation, open interest, hedging, curve slope
Demand forecasts too high, efficiency from high prices, shale technology
Do low prices cure themselves; OPEC management; supply disruptions
Disruptions fade, 2 mb/d swing, 2015 oversupply, OPEC response
Marginal cost, stability by chance, inelastic demand, storage
Product world, BTU dislocation, project economics, marginal barrel, volatility
LNG contracts, gas vs oil subsidy, dollar and China pricing
Subsidy reform kills marginal demand; close

completeness_estimate: 0.87 - first reader captured the curve, demand-forecast, shale, OPEC, storage, refining and LNG arguments; missed the fading-disruption detail, storage lag, Korean refinery exports, the oil-indexed gas pass-through, Asian contract-honouring and the closing humility remark; two minor over-fills (disruption size, cheap-crude reason).

claims.speaker: Moderator (Energy Intelligence panel chair)
claims.quote: these two markets are sympathetic not parallel if you've watched the WTI rent spread over the last couple years they tend to Trend
claims.claim: Brent and WTI are sympathetic not parallel markets; their spread tends to trend, with different characteristics (Cushing delivery location).

claims.speaker: Moderator (Energy Intelligence panel chair)
claims.quote: volumes have been relatively stable even with the increase in open interest which is highly unusual
claims.claim: Crude futures open interest rose strongly over five years (peak about 4 million lots) with stable volume, partly from banks exiting and more direct hedger use.
claims.indicator: crude oil futures open interest and volume

claims.speaker: Moderator (Energy Intelligence panel chair)
claims.quote: open interest has come off in Long liquidation
claims.claim: In the 2014 price fall open interest dropped (long liquidation), then rose again when Brent broke 90, read as new shorts entering plus more hedging.
claims.testable: yes: open interest and price regression

claims.speaker: Moderator (Energy Intelligence panel chair)
claims.quote: people are doing a guaranteed Revenue enhancements
claims.claim: Independent US producers bought put options and structured guaranteed revenue hedges after the fall, contract and bank obligations forcing them to hedge.

claims.speaker: Moderator (Energy Intelligence panel chair)
claims.quote: it's not necessarily the spot price but the slope of the Curve
claims.claim: For a merchant the slope of the curve matters more than spot: Brent moved from steep backwardation to contango, which pays to store oil and starts stockpiling.

claims.speaker: Moderator (Energy Intelligence panel chair)
claims.quote: all the volatilities in the front end of the market not the back end of the market
claims.claim: WTI volatility is in the front end while the back end still carries a premium for 3-7 year oil over spot.

claims.speaker: Chris (Vitol, physical oil merchant)
claims.quote: forecast Demand versus actual demand has continued to under
claims.claim: Agencies (IEA, OPEC, DOE) forecast 1.1-1.2 mb/d demand growth while actual is about 0.6 mb/d, so forecasts overstate demand and are revised down month by month.

claims.speaker: Chris (Vitol, physical oil merchant)
claims.quote: the sustained period of over 100 oil for three years has done is is is
claims.claim: Three years of oil above $100 produced efficiency gains (vessels with 15% lower fuel burn, US car fleet efficiency, 787/A380 aircraft) that lower demand, so high prices cure high prices.

claims.speaker: Chris (Vitol, physical oil merchant)
claims.quote: reduction in incremental Gasol demand gas oil demand obviously is a driver
claims.claim: Chinese gasoil demand growth, a proxy for construction activity, has dropped sharply, signalling the Chinese slowdown.

claims.speaker: Chris (Vitol, physical oil merchant)
claims.quote: the preponderance of Technology on new production or unconventional production
claims.claim: Shale technology lifts oil recovered per rig (Bakken) and cuts costs, so supply growth accelerates and is cost-effective.

claims.speaker: Chris (Vitol, physical oil merchant)
claims.quote: relative value of hydrocarbon versus gas and and the alternative
claims.claim: Rising LNG, LPG and ethane exports from the Gulf Coast displace crude in petrochemicals, adding to the demand story.

claims.speaker: Moderator (Energy Intelligence panel chair)
claims.quote: high prices cure high prices uh low prices cure low prices
claims.claim: Commodity merchants' adage: high prices cure high prices and low prices cure low prices; the question is whether the low price will cure itself.

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: I think that it's going to go a lot more lower before it begins to cure itself
claims.claim: Oil will fall much lower before low prices cure themselves, a traffic jam analogy: pain is needed before a traffic cop (OPEC) steps in, taking six to nine months.

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: it was a beautiful management of the market it was not where the prices belonged that era is gone
claims.claim: The $100-110 oil price was managed by Saudi/OPEC supply, helped by Iran sanctions and Libya, and not an equilibrium; prices should fall another $20-30.

claims.speaker: Pierre/Peter (hedge fund oil trader, caption spelling varies)
claims.quote: we lost um you know a day of production
claims.claim: Oil stayed at $110 for 3.5 years because about 2 mb/d of supply disruption (Libya, Syria, Iraq, Iran sanctions) offset US shale growth while OPEC covered about 1 mb/d annual demand growth from spare capacity.
claims.indicator: supply disruptions vs US shale growth

correction.issue: The size of the supply disruption is not stated: the caption reads 'we lost a day of production' with no number, so '2 mb/d' is the first reader's guess (it is also not consistent with the Libya, Syria and Iran losses named). The speaker's point is that the disruptions and US shale growth were of similar size and cancelled out, with OPEC's spare capacity meeting about 1 mb/d of annual demand growth.
correction.fix: Oil held near $110 for 3.5 years because Arab Spring and sanctions-related supply disruptions (Libya, Syria, Iraq, Iran, from 2010 to early 2014) were offset by a roughly equal rise in US shale output, while OPEC met demand growth of about 1 mb/d per year from spare capacity left after the financial crisis.

claims.speaker: Pierre/Peter (hedge fund oil trader, caption spelling varies)
claims.quote: we had roughly 2 million swing uh in Supply demand balance from June to now and that's why prices came off
claims.claim: From June to autumn 2014 the balance swung by about 2 mb/d (US supply 1.7 vs 1.3 expected, Libya +0.5, demand 0.6 vs 1.3-1.4 expected) and prices fell.

claims.speaker: Pierre/Peter (hedge fund oil trader, caption spelling varies)
claims.quote: we should have at least a two million buyers a day oversupply next year
claims.claim: With US shale up 1.5 mb/d, Libya steady, Iran up and Brazil up, 2015 oversupply is at least 2 mb/d, which cannot persist because storage fills within six months, so prices must adjust.

claims.speaker: Pierre/Peter (hedge fund oil trader, caption spelling varies)
claims.quote: they would just shoot themselves in the food by keep on cutting production
claims.claim: OPEC alone cutting 2 mb/d each year would lose share to US shale and not stop price falls; stabilising needs slower US growth or new disruptions.

claims.speaker: Pierre/Peter (hedge fund oil trader, caption spelling varies)
claims.quote: when I look at you know marginal cost of production of shaylord and I look at what people were saying in natural gas in 2008
claims.claim: Marginal cost falls with technology: natural gas was said to need $7 in 2008 and now $3, so shale oil's marginal cost will also fall, implying a bear market.

claims.speaker: Pierre/Peter (hedge fund oil trader, caption spelling varies)
claims.quote: there's not no like stable oil price that can last for the next 10 years
claims.claim: The three-year stability was by chance (masking disruptions); expect cycles of lower and higher prices, lower first, then lower prices cut supply growth and revive demand, planting the next rally.

claims.speaker: Pierre/Peter (hedge fund oil trader, caption spelling varies)
claims.quote: demand is so inelastic if we basically um ten percent move in the price it has an impact of maybe 0.15 percent
claims.claim: Short-run oil demand is very inelastic: a 10% price move shifts demand about 0.15%, so price must move a lot to rebalance.

claims.speaker: Chris (Vitol, physical oil merchant)
claims.quote: I think of storage as Arbitrage levels
claims.claim: Contango allows storage arbitrage; financing is available (banks are not a constraint), but logistics limit storage and VLCC availability is finite and short-term.
claims.conditions: contango wide enough to cover costs

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: 80 85 percent of the new
claims.claim: Asian refining is oversupplied and under pressure; 80-85% of new refinery investment is government strategic, so private firms compete with non-economic decision makers.

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: you have a whole country which was the demand of 700 000 per day
claims.claim: Australia's refining system is likely to shut down, turning it into a product importer, a surprise for product trade flows.

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: that has a shelf life to three four five seven years
claims.claim: US refineries benefit from cheap crude but the advantage has a shelf life of three to seven years.

correction.issue: 'Benefit from cheap crude' is not in the transcript: the speaker says US refiners are doing well, being the best refineries and operators with a Gulf Coast location, and that this has a shelf life of three to seven years, with some pain later but much less severe than Europe's.
correction.fix: US refiners are doing very well now because they are among the best refineries and operators with a Gulf Coast location, but the advantage has a shelf life of three to seven years; some pain will come later, much less than Europe's.

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: we are moving to more of more of a product world than a crude world
claims.claim: Large exporters like Aramco may have more products than crude, shifting pricing power from crude to products.

claims.speaker: Chris (Vitol, physical oil merchant)
claims.quote: the Arbitrage between Eastern gas and and U.S gas three dollars versus 16 15 to 19 per M and BTU is is is is is unsustainable
claims.claim: The arbitrage between Asian gas ($15-19/mmBtu) and US gas ($3) and the BTU value dislocation between crude, gas and coal is unsustainable and will reshape refining and LPG economics.

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: you look at the price of oil of 60 70 a barrel very few of them make sense today
claims.claim: At $60-70 oil few new projects (Canada, Africa, Russia) are economic, constraining future supply; renewables need higher subsidies.

claims.speaker: Chris (Vitol, physical oil merchant)
claims.quote: it's a constant reshuffle of the deck and I I don't think it's fair to say that any one barrel is is the marginal Barrel
claims.claim: No single barrel (West African etc.) is the marginal barrel; supply constantly reshuffles regionally.

claims.speaker: Moderator (Energy Intelligence panel chair)
claims.quote: people so many banks exit the business there's no volatility there's no fun anymore so no fun is coming back
claims.claim: Volatility had been low after banks exited trading; it is returning in late 2014.

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: in oil you can change your mind but in thus you cannot change your mind
claims.claim: Gas is like marriage and oil like dating: LNG volumes are sold under long contracts, so US LNG will come regardless of price and oil-indexed contracts last to 2035, creating dual markets.

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: the subsidy that oil gives to gas will disappear and gas prices have to go up to carry their own weight
claims.claim: With low oil prices the oil-linked subsidy to gas disappears and gas prices must rise, so US gas could become more expensive than oil-indexed gas; LPG adjusts immediately.

claims.speaker: Chris (Vitol, physical oil merchant)
claims.quote: that's been partially offset at least with a lot of emerging market economies with the rise in the relative value of the dollar
claims.claim: Dollar strength offset the crude price collapse in emerging markets, so expected demand elasticity has not yet appeared.
claims.indicator: USD vs oil price in local currency

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: in China the price of oil is set by the state it is Market linked but if the prices tomorrow go down uh the state will take some of the prices down but not rapidly
claims.claim: China adjusts domestic fuel prices slowly, so demand response to lower oil is delayed.

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: the lower oil prices give the ability to deregulate and that kills a great deal of Demand by itself
claims.claim: India and Indonesia use low oil prices to deregulate fuel prices, so consumers face market prices and marginal demand from subsidised economies does not arrive.

claims.speaker: Pierre/Peter (hedge fund oil trader, caption spelling varies)
claims.quote: so far we haven't had Supply disruption from Iraq despite what's going on with Isis
claims.claim: Supply disruptions that had propped up the 2011-14 price are fading: Libya returned unexpectedly, Iran sanctions eased, Iraq (despite ISIS) and Russia (despite Ukraine) have not lost output, and the Russia sanctions may have hit European demand rather than supply, so geopolitical headlines did not tighten supply in 2014.
claims.indicator: Libyan, Iranian, Iraqi and Russian crude output; supply disruption total
claims.direction: bearish oil as disruption premium fades
claims.conditions: when geopolitical events do not actually remove barrels
claims.testable: yes - compare disruption volumes with price changes

claims.speaker: Chris (Vitol, physical oil merchant)
claims.quote: if you get the right pricing incentive the market will react and store um we haven't seen a huge amount of it yet but uh it feels like it could go that way especially by q1 next year
claims.claim: Contango storage arbitrage responds to the pricing incentive with a lag: little oil had gone into storage yet, but it could build by the first quarter of 2015 if the curve keeps paying for storage.
claims.indicator: Brent contango; commercial and floating storage
claims.direction: stock builds when contango exceeds storage cost
claims.conditions: storage cost and financing available (financing is not the constraint)

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: some of the best refineries in the world which are in Korea for example they have heavily invested in upgrading but they have to export fifty percent uh at least of their products
claims.claim: Even high-quality Asian refiners (Korea) must export at least half their output, and with gasoline-oriented capacity, a slowdown in Chinese and Indian demand growth and new refineries about to start in Abu Dhabi and Saudi Arabia, Asian refining margins are under pressure before the new capacity even arrives.
claims.indicator: Asian refining margins; Korean product exports; China and India demand growth
claims.conditions: new capacity commissioning while demand slows
claims.testable: yes - refining margins versus capacity additions

claims.speaker: Panelist (speaker not clear in captions)
claims.quote: whatever happens whatever we say here something else will happen
claims.claim: Forecasts, however well reasoned, are overtaken by new events, so something will change; that is the nature of trading and a reason to run risk control rather than rely on a single supply-demand scenario.

claims.speaker: Chris (Vitol, physical oil merchant)
claims.quote: well naturally anything priced off the crude Market is is obviously going to be lower but uh yeah I mean that's not that's not enough at this point
claims.claim: Lower crude cuts the price of oil-indexed gas automatically but not enough to close the gap between Asian and US gas, so the regional gas arbitrage will have to adjust further and affects the economics of new projects.
claims.indicator: oil-indexed LNG price versus US gas; Asia gas premium
claims.testable: yes - oil-indexed formula against spot gas

claims.speaker: Dr. Fesharaki (caption: the good doctor; energy consultant)
claims.quote: Asians actually are very polite they have not there's not one arbitration of one court case in any LNG deal in 40 years
claims.claim: Asian LNG buyers honour long-term contracts (no arbitration or court case in 40 years), unlike European buyers, so dual oil-indexed and spot gas prices can persist for years and US LNG volumes already sold are safe despite lower oil.
claims.indicator: LNG contract disputes; oil-indexed vs spot gas price gap
claims.conditions: buyers accept contract duality when contracts are long-term and indexed
claims.testable: partly - dispute history is checkable, persistence of dual prices is a forecast
